activation.note: Activation targets choosing or changing wagon feature names, not implementation, description-only edits, or artifact naming. Task terms and file kinds are directly observable; name-change detection explicitly needs a new observer and planning-phase classification is honestly labeled as judgment.

audit.summary: All fourteen segments survive at their claimed destinations, including the ordered naming procedure, type choices, examples, term definition, and audit metadata. The single naming obligation remains intact; added rationale, cross-reference, example labels, and activation framing are declared, and application-specific examples are inherited from the source rather than imposed as constraints.

segmentChecks.note: The given/when establish the wagon feature-naming context, and then retains artifact seeding, type-specific verb selection, domain-or-resource object selection, and {verb}-{object} composition.
All five ordered steps survive in prefer, including all four artifact types, the domain OR resource choice, and kebab-case formatting.
The data example and its make-choice result are retained verbatim in prefer[5].
The state example and its track-timebank result are retained verbatim in prefer[6].
The event example and its start-match result are retained verbatim in prefer[7].
Then explicitly defines the feature seed as a produce/consume artifact from which the feature name is derived.

risks: If a wagon has several produce/consume artifacts, no seed-selection tie-break is supplied; this is also absent from the source, so any artifact-derived choice following the steps remains compliant.
The allowed verbs are not enumerated here; the planner must follow the explicit pointer to planner.feature.verb-selection-by-artifact-type rather than rely on this rule alone.

unobservable: change (feature added or feature renamed): explicitly needs a new diff-level observer
phase (planning): explicitly llm_judged rather than directly observable by a Datalog engine

review.summary: The rewrite preserves the complete naming procedure, all examples, and the feature-seed definition without changing the obligation. A weak planner can follow the coder-facing steps, with only the source-inherited multi-artifact choice and external verb-list dependency requiring attention; activation is not fully deterministic because change detection and planning phase are not currently observable facts.
